description.narrative:
Artivism Without Borders is a youth-led cooperation project between PLACE Network (France) and KQ Hub Africa (Uganda), connecting young refugee and migrant-background artivists (18–35) through participatory arts and cross-continental peer exchange. The project creates a structured space where young people collaborate as equal partners to co-develop artistic work that challenges harmful migration narratives and strengthens cultural bridges between Africa and Europe.
Through peer-learning sessions, Artivism Labs, and public showcases, participants will produce performances, exhibitions, or digital storytelling grounded in lived experience. Each showcase will include facilitated dialogue with cultural and civic stakeholders, using art as an entry point to discuss inclusion practices, cultural access, and artistic mobility. The project builds sustainable cooperation by establishing a lasting peer network and tested collaboration formats that can continue beyond the grant period.
The project aims to strengthen cooperation between Uganda and France by connecting around 20 young refugee and migrant-background artivists through a joint participatory arts process. It will create a structured space where young people in both contexts exchange practices, co-develop creative work, and collaborate as equal partners on shared challenges linked to migration, inclusion, and representation.
In the short term, the project will strengthen participants’ skills in storytelling, collaboration, and civic engagement through Artivism Labs and peer-learning exchanges between Uganda and France. These sessions will support youth to develop creative outputs (performances, exhibitions, and digital storytelling) while also exploring how art can be used to influence public narratives and engage institutions.
The project will culminate in one main public showcase event in each country, combining artistic presentation with facilitated exchange involving cultural, media, and civic stakeholders. This will increase the visibility of youth perspectives and create concrete opportunities for engagement beyond the project circle.
In the longer term, the project will leave behind tested cooperation formats and a cross-continental peer network that participants and both organisations can continue using beyond the grant period. This will strengthen youth-led Africa–Europecultural cooperation and support longer-term inclusion of refugee youth in cultural and civic ecosystems.

participating-org.narrative:
PLACE Network is building a future where people with migration backgrounds are recognised as drivers of innovation, leadership, andchange. Through challenging narratives, meaningful inclusion, and systemic transformation, we ensure diverse representation is not the exception but the standard across all spheres of society.
PLACE is a migrant-led organisation with a strong youth-led approach,meaning people with migration backgrounds, predominantly young leaders, hold decision-making roles, inform strategic direction, andlead our programmes. We apply an intersectional lens, recognising migration as a diverse, multi-dimensional experience shaped by individual realities.
Our mission is to create pathways for change by equipping individuals, institutions, and systems to act. Through tailored programmes, partnerships, and initiatives, we empower people with migration backgrounds—alongside public and private actors, to challenge outdated narratives and co-create practical, sustainable solutions for inclusion, equality, and leadership.
Our impact focuses on four main sectors: business, entrepreneurship, media <(>&<)> arts, and public leadership, across Europe and Africa. Our key actions include fellowships and leadership development, capacity-building, inclusive dialogue and collaboration with local actors, advocacy and narrative change, mentoring and networking, and opportunities-sharing.
PLACE is grounded in three core values: Human Rights and Social Justice, Diversity and Inclusion, and Engagement andParticipation, ensuring people with migration backgrounds are empowered as equal partners and decision-makers. We are committed to safeguarding and duty of care to ensure participation is safe, inclusive, and meaningful
